primary_claim: Red-teaming gpt-oss-20b with a jailbreak that repeats a compliant-sounding CoT-mimicry template finds the model highly robust to black-box jailbreaks overall, but attack success rate is non-monotonic in the number of repetitions: it rises with more repeats, peaks around ~1000 repetitions (13 percentage points above a single-repeat baseline), then declines with further repetitions, reaching ~85% ASR when combined with 8 prompt rewordings and retries

effect.metric: jailbreak attack success rate (ASR) vs. number of CoT-mimicry repetitions
effect.value: ASR increases by 13 percentage points at ~1000 repeats vs. a single-repeat baseline, then declines with more repetitions; ~85% ASR with 1024 repeats combined with 8 prompt rewordings and retries

contradicts_or_qualifies: Anil et al. (2024) many-shot jailbreaking scaling law showing a smooth upward ASR curve with more repeats; this work instead finds ASR peaks around 1000 repetitions and then declines
limitations_stated: this red-teaming sprint may include small metric inaccuracies
the LLM judge (gemini-2.5-flash-lite) appears to underreport attack success rate, sometimes fooled by disclaimers accompanying harmful content
uses a relaxed definition of jailbreak success (non-trivial harmful info even if framed as educational); a stricter definition would yield much lower ASR
did not benchmark this jailbreak against other state-of-the-art jailbreaks
policy-mention statistics may under-report true frequency since some implicit policy references may not have been correctly decoded
quote: Counterintuitively, we discovered that attack effectiveness peaks at around 1000 repetitions, then decreases with more repetitions.
